title: Conformance Lattice: SLO-aware Quant Intake and Regression Rollback Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a repeatable, auditable intake and publishing flow for quantization artifacts (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) that is driven by a conformance lattice: progressive checks that combine accuracy, latency, memory, and SLO alignment. The playbook implements automated smoke gates, metric contracts, and an automated rollback policy which is SLO-aware (not just delta-based) so we avoid promoting variants that regress downstream SLA-sensitive customers. The goal is to reduce manual review friction while providing deterministic signals for safe rollouts and fast remediation.
acceptance_criteria: A. New quant artifact uploaded to staging triggers an end-to-end intake pipeline (profiling, calibration check, perf microbench, eval suite) without manual steps.

B. Each artifact publishes a standardized performance JSON that includes: p50/p95 latency at target batch sizes, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, accuracy deltas on canonical evals, and a computed SLO-impact score.
C. Canary rollout automation evaluates the artifact against live shadow traffic for at least 1 hour and produces a regression verdict based on the conformance lattice thresholds.
D. If SLO-impact score > threshold OR accuracy drop > 1.5% absolute OR latency regression > 20% on p95, the artifact is automatically demoted and a rollback action is recorded in the release log.
E. Console surfaces per-variant timeline, telemetry links, and an explicit human-approve gate for manual override, including reason and reviewer name.
F. Documentation and integration tests for the intake flow exist and pass in CI (unit + smoke integration harness).
proposed_flow: 1) Artifact upload: model + quant metadata + reference eval set pointer
2) Local profile stage: run perf microbench on target allocator and batch sizes
3) Calibration validation: run a small calibration pass for INT8/AWQ/FP8 and record metric deltas
4) Canonical evals: run accuracy/regression suite against release baselines
5) SLO-impact scoring: combine latency, accuracy, and memory into a single risk score
6) Publish perf JSON to catalog and mark as candidate
7) Shadow canary: route non-production traffic using canary policy for 1h (metrics + traces), compute drift
8) Verdicting: auto-promote, auto-demote, or require human approval based on lattice
9) If promoted, pin variant to a rollout plan with staged percentages and rollback thresholds
implementation_notes: - Use existing perf harness infra from ENG-33458 for microbench and memory profiling.
- Extend telemetry schema (ingest) to include 'slo_impact_score' and 'variant_lattice_flags' so Console can filter variants by risk.
- Reuse and augment the 'pin registry' to track provenance: source artifact hash, quant toolchain (bitsandbytes/gptq/awq-version), and CI hash.
- Integrate with Rollout service to schedule staged percentages and attach automatic rollback webhooks.
- Add explicit audit entry in customer-facing audit logs for any promoted/demoted artifact when customers run private deployments.
risk_tradeoffs: - Strict lattice thresholds reduce incidents but may block useful low-cost variants; provide an 'experimental' channel for high-risk variants.
- Shadow canaries increase cost (duplicate traffic) but provide the highest-fidelity signal for SLO impact; limit to selected high-traffic models initially.
- Automated rollback is high-value for availability but must be conservative to avoid flip-flopping; add debounce windows and manual override hooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dev-only ingestion and edge-case fuzzing (1 week)
Phase 1: Controlled canary on non-production traffic for 2 models (INT8 and GPTQ) (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Broader catalog publishing with 'experimental' flag and limited customer opt-in (4 weeks)
Phase 3: Default catalog availability with SLO-aware auto-rollout for low-risk variants (6 weeks)
Rollback policy: immediate demotion if SLO-impact score breaches threshold for >5 minutes or repeated accuracy failures are observed
metrics_and_contracts: Telemetry keys required: slo_impact_score, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, peak_gpu_mb, accuracy_delta_pct
Thresholds (initial): accuracy_delta_pct > -1.5 => fail, p95_latency_ms increase > 20% => fail, slo_impact_score > 0.35 => fail
Canary sampling: minimum 1000 requests or 1 hour whichever comes later
Alerting: Prometheus+PagerDuty rule for any promoted variant that later crosses safety thresholds in production
